objective: Establish how HolyAgent can ship an @opentui/solid 0.8.x setup TUI given how its CLI is built and run, so the TUI works from both the Claude plugin and the Pi package on macOS, Linux and Windows.
scope: HolyAgent repo (read-only): /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3branch. How the CLI is built and shipped: packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts and packages/integrations/pi/src/generate.ts (bundling packages/runtime into dist/scripts/holyagent.js), the wrapper dist/scripts/holyagent and bun-flags.ts, the Claude plugin layout (is there any node_modules at runtime?), packages/integrations/pi/package.json (dependencies installed by pi install npm:...), packages/runtime/src/cli/setup.ts (the setup command and its flags), bunfig.toml and mise.toml.

OpenTUI (github.com/sst/opentui or its current home; npm @opentui/core and @opentui/solid at the newest 0.8.x): how @opentui/core loads its native renderer (bun:ffi dlopen of a per-platform package such as @opentui/core-darwin-arm64, embedded asset, or WASM), whether Bun.build can bundle it into one JS file and with what (an asset, a plugin, external), the Solid JSX transform it needs (bun plugin, babel preset, tsconfig jsxImportSource) and whether that works in a bun build bundle, its headless test renderer API, and its Bun version requirement.

Answer: which shipping options work (A: bundle everything into holyagent.js with the native library as an embedded file; B: keep OpenTUI external and resolve it from an installed package such as the Pi package node_modules, with a plain line-based fallback when it is absent; C: install it on first use with bun add into a cache; any other), with the evidence for each and the trade-offs for size, offline use, Windows and the dependency updater (mise run deps:update moves package.json caret ranges and bun.lock).

result:
result: Option A works only as a compiled executable, or as a bundle plus native-library sidecar that HolyAgent's bundler does not emit today. Option B works for Pi but needs a new dependency path, and the Claude plugin has no node_modules. Option C works wherever Bun and the network are available, but needs a pinned install cache. I recommend B or C with a line-based fallback, and A only if you accept a per-platform binary.

- Is the shipped CLI allowed to stop being one platform-neutral `holyagent.js` (the Option A cost)?

**Sourced facts: OpenTUI** (npm registry, fetched 2026-11-09)
- Latest `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` are both 0.8.3 (updated 2026-11-07), and the repo is now github.com/anomalyco/opentui.
- Core's dependencies are bun-ffi-structs 0.3.1, diff 9.0.0, marked 17.0.1 and string-width 7.2.0, with peer `web-tree-sitter` 0.25.10. Solid depends on core 0.8.3, @babel/core, babel-preset-solid 1.9.16, @babel/preset-typescript, babel-plugin-module-resolver and s-js, with peer `solid-js ^1.9.12`.
- The renderer is native Zig, called through FFI (opentui.com/packages/opentui-core). Bun loads the matching optional per-platform package: `@opentui/core-{darwin,linux,win32}-{x64,arm64}`, plus `-musl` variants on Linux (opentui.com/docs/getting-started/runtime-support).
- Older `zig.ts` (commit 406bed2) does `import(\`@opentui/core-${process.platform}-${process.arch}/index.ts\`)` and then `bun:ffi` `dlopen(path)`. That package's default export is the library path. This is an old commit, so the current code may differ.
- Importing core loads no native code. `createCliRenderer()` loads it (runtime-support page).
- Bun requirement is 1.3.14 or later, and 1.4.0 or later on Windows arm64. Node needs 26.4 or later with `--experimental-ffi` (runtime-support page).
- `bun build --compile` can embed the native library, parser worker, grammars and tree-sitter WASM. You should set `define: {"process.env.OPENTUI_LIBC": ...}` at build time, and the matching native package must be installed on the build machine (opentui.com/docs/reference/standalone-executables). The deploy page says a plain "Bun bundle" must ship "every emitted asset or external dependency".
- Bun issue #30717 (2026-05-14): on canary 1.3.14, `dlopen` of an embedded `with {type:"file"}` library in a compiled binary failed with a raw `/$bunfs/...` path. The issue says the cause was a stub in Bun's Rust port and that a fix was filed as #30720. I did not confirm the fix is released. Issue #29585 says Workers extract the embedded `.so` to /tmp and never clean it up.
- Solid needs a JSX transform with `moduleName: "@opentui/solid", generate: "universal"` (babel-preset-solid). It is installed with the `@opentui/solid/bun-plugin` Bun build plugin, or with a `bunfig.toml` `preload` of `@opentui/solid/preload`.
- The README's `Bun.build` example passes `plugins: [solidPlugin]` and `compile`. The Solid transform skips anything under `node_modules`, so only HolyAgent's own `.tsx` gets transformed.
- `@opentui/solid` exports `testRender(node, {width, height})`. It returns a setup with `renderOnce()`, `captureCharFrame()`, `renderer.destroy()`, and keyboard and mouse input. It runs under `bun:test` and needs no TTY.
- `@opentui/core/testing` (the Core test renderer) works on both Bun and Node.

**Sourced facts: HolyAgent** (`/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3branch`)
- The Claude CLI is built by `packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts:213-219` (`bundleModule`, `target: "bun"`, source `packages/runtime/src/cli/main.ts` per line 35).
- `packages/runtime/src/bundle.ts:50` calls `Bun.build({entrypoints, target, format: "esm", external})` with no plugins and no define. Line 55-57 returns only `outputs[0].text()`, so any extra emitted asset is dropped.
- The Claude plugin ships generated files only (`generate.ts:221-236`): `scripts/holyagent`, `empty-bunfig.toml` and `holyagent.js`. No node_modules is generated, and a glob of `packages/integrations/*/dist/**/node_modules` found none.
- Hooks run `bun --no-env-file --config=${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/empty-bunfig.toml holyagent.js ...` (`generate.ts:110-122`). The `wrapper.sh:44` `exec` line uses the same flags, so `bunfig.toml` `preload` is disabled at runtime.
- The Pi runtime is `pi/src/generate.ts:47,131-137`, bundled for Bun from `hooks/pi-entry.ts` and wrapped through `bunFlags` (`bun-flags.ts:11-14`). The Pi extension is bundled for Node, with Pi's host modules external (`generate.ts:112-119`).
- The Pi package manifest has `peerDependencies` only and no `dependencies`, on purpose (`generate.ts:78-82`). The reason given is that Pi would install every dependency whatever the config says.
- `setup.ts:42` defines `setup [--scope ...] [--undo] [--dry-run] [--subagent-cache-ttl ...] [--skip-ctx7]`. It is stateless and returns report lines through `Verbatim` (`setup.ts:24-25,76-77`), so a TUI would be a new interactive mode beside that line-based output.
- `bunfig.toml` has only `[lint]` and `[fmt]`. `mise.toml:91,95` runs `scripts/update-dependencies.ts` and I did not read it.

**Options (evidence plus inference)**
- **A (bundle into `holyagent.js`)**
  - Plain `Bun.build` bundling is not documented to embed the library as one file. OpenTUI's docs promise embedding only for `--compile`, and for a plain bundle they say to ship the emitted assets.
  - HolyAgent would need a plugin option in `bundleModule` (for the Solid plugin), a build-time define for libc, and all eight native packages installed at build time (`bun install --os="*" --cpu="*"`).
  - A single cross-platform JS file cannot hold one native library per platform without extraction code. Inference: loading and libc selection would need custom code.
  - Size grows by about 7 MB (core's unpacked size, May 2026) plus the native libraries for each platform.
  - The embedded-library `dlopen` bug (#30717) is a risk on Bun 1.3.14 canary.
  - A compiled executable per platform is documented and works offline, but it replaces the Bun-run `holyagent.js` model and the hook command.
- **B (external, resolved from an installed package)**
  - This works wherever node_modules exists with `@opentui/core`, the matching native package and `solid-js`.
  - The Claude plugin has none, so B alone gives it only the fallback.
  - Pi's peer dependencies do not install OpenTUI. A `dependencies` entry would reverse the choice at `pi/src/generate.ts:78-82`.
  - This is the smallest change and works offline once installed. Windows needs the `core-win32-x64` or `core-win32-arm64` package.
  - Because `holyagent.js` is precompiled, the Solid transform has to run at HolyAgent's build time, which `bundleModule` does not support today.
- **C (`bun add` into a cache on first use)**
  - This works wherever Bun and the network are available, and gives the same result on all three operating systems.
  - It fails offline and needs a pinned version, because `deps:update` moves caret ranges in `package.json` and `bun.lock` and would not see a cache. Inference: pin exact versions in one HolyAgent-owned file, or the updater cannot keep it current.

notes: Pin `solid-js` at 1.9.16 or later (Solid docs). A TUI interface should carry a `--no-tui` or non-TTY fallback, because OpenTUI needs a native renderer.
